title: Two ears, two times
hook: A tiny timing difference can carry direction.

knows: Animals can act and respond to conditions.
doesNotKnow: In a toy model a sound reaches the left ear at 4 ms and the right ear at 6 ms. Which ear receives it first?

misconception: One observed behavior always supports a broad or causal conclusion.
objective: In a toy model a sound reaches the left ear at 4 ms and the right ear at 6 ms. Which ear receives it first?

claims.text: In a toy model a sound reaches the left ear at 4 ms and the right ear at 6 ms. Which ear receives it first? The stipulated arrival times are 4 ms at the left ear and 6 ms at the right ear: left is earlier by 2 ms. Some animals can use differences between ears as directional cues. These values are invented for the comparison, not measured sensory thresholds.
claims.source: Stipulated toy observations; not observed animal data. Source lead, not checked: OpenStax Biology 2e, Behavioral Biology, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/45-7-behavioral-biology

claims.text: The panels show a stipulated illustrative scenario, not observations or measurements of real animals.
In a new toy case a sound reaches the right ear at 3 ms and the left ear at 5 ms. Which receives it first? 3 ms is earlier than 5 ms.
